question: If the mean, mode and quartile deviation of a distribution is 2, 7 and 3, respectively, then Karl Pearson's coefficient of skewness is given by:
solution:
The correct answer is (**- 10/9). **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 Skewness (Sk) = {(Mean - Mode)} over S.D.

The relationship between Standard Deviation (S.D) and Quartile Deviation (Q.D) is: S. D. = {3over 2}times Q.D. 

Therefore, Skewness (Sk) = {(Mean - Mode)} over {{3over 2} times Q. D.}Or, Sk = {3 (2 - 7)} over {{3over 2} times 3}

Or, Sk = -10/9

**Karl Pearson's coefficient of skewness is (-10/9). **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** There are two formulas, that were developed by Karl Pearson, available to calculate the coefficient of skewness. One uses the mode while the other uses the mean. 

 
• Using Mean: Skewness (Sk) = {(Mean - Mode)} over S.D.
 
• Using Median: Skewness (Sk) = {3(Mean - Median)} over S.D.
